subject.title: Telegram should default to allowlist mode with owner ID

question: Should fresh Telegram setup switch from pairing-first to token-verified owner allowlist capture, and what compatibility rule should protect existing pairing-mode configs?
rationale: The change improves a security default but changes first-run trust, setup UX, and default authorization behavior, so code inspection alone cannot choose the permanent product contract.

options.title: Token-verified fresh-setup allowlist
options.body: Generate a short setup token, capture only the Telegram sender who sends that token, write dmPolicy="allowlist" with that numeric owner ID, and leave explicit pairing configs unchanged.

options.title: Keep pairing default and improve guidance
options.body: Keep current pairing behavior but make docs/setup warnings stronger and steer one-owner users toward manual allowFrom configuration.

options.title: Defer to cross-channel auto-flip
options.body: Do not change Telegram setup yet and resolve the broader post-bootstrap owner-derived default policy in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/81876 first.

recommendation.title: Token-verified fresh-setup allowlist
recommendation.body: Generate a short setup token, capture only the Telegram sender who sends that token, write dmPolicy="allowlist" with that numeric owner ID, and leave explicit pairing configs unchanged.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent history covers the current Telegram default, runtime fallback, setup path, and docs most directly tied to this product decision.
